title: Dynamic Commitment Ledger and Role-Timeboxing Protocol
creator: Alejandra Park
description:
Problem: As cycles grow in scope we lack a single, auditable way to record partial team commitments, temporary role allocations, and forced scope slices. Current triage notes live in ephemeral docs and Slack threads; that friction delays mid-cycle rebalances and creates confusion during cross-team handoffs.

Proposed change: Introduce a lightweight 'Commitment Ledger' and an accompanying Role-Timeboxing Protocol. The ledger is an operational artifact (not a replacement for OKRs) where PMs and Eng leads publish per-cycle timeboxed commitments by role (e.g., 0.4 FE for two weeks). The Role-Timeboxing Protocol defines how to create, adjust, and surface those commitments to staffing dashboards and the cycle cadence (planning, mid-cycle trim, and hotfix lanes).

Goals: 
- Reduce coordination overhead for mid-cycle staff swaps by 30% (measured by time to confirm reassignments).
- Make scope-cut decisions visible and reversible (audit trail for who approved each cut).
- Provide deterministic signals to Capacity and Platform teams for rebalancing (automated alerts when committed headcount delta > 0.2 FTE for 10+ business days).

Scope: Minimum Viable Ledger (MVP) will include a canonical ledger record per initiative, a small UI table inside Console Ops (read-only for most users, editable by PM/Tech lead), and a set of rules that convert ledger entries into signals for the staffing dashboard and the mid-cycle triage checklist. No heavy RBAC or billing integration in MVP.
acceptance_criteria: A ledger entry can be created for any CycleOps initiative with fields: role, fraction (decimal FTE), start_date, end_date, approval_by (PM or Eng lead), and rationale.
UI: Entries are visible in the Console Ops staff panel and filterable by role, team, and time range.
Signals: Ledger changes trigger a Capacity Dashboard alert if net committed delta exceeds configured thresholds for >10 business days.
Audit trail: Every change to a ledger entry writes a change comment that includes user, timestamp, and short reason, stored as part of the initiative history.
Process docs: A one-page Role-Timeboxing Protocol is published on Confluence and linked from the ledger UI.
No customer-facing API changes in MVP; internal API for the staffing dashboard only.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng leads and PM guild. Agreed to keep ledger schema intentionally small to accelerate adoption.
2026-03-04: Design sync — proposed UI table mockups sketched; Ricardo (Design) recommended inline approval flow to reduce round trips.
2026-03-06: Engineering feasibility review — backend events and immutable history are straightforward; estimated 4 dev days + 1 QA day for integration with staffing dashboard.
2026-03-08: Stakeholder review — Platform team requested retention policy and export for capacity forecasting (added to follow-ups).
2026-03-10: Decision: Ship MVP without export; schedule export for post-MVP sprint if adoption metrics warrant it.
risks: Teams treat ledger as a commitment contract and resist flexible changes — mitigated by training doc and required approval field for changes.
Noise: small, transient assignments create alert fatigue — mitigated by thresholding alerts to sustained deltas (>10 business days).
Data parity: discrepancies between ledger and timesheet systems could erode trust — plan to validate with a 2-week pilot and manual reconciliation.
next_steps: Publish single-page Role-Timeboxing Protocol and circulate to PM/Eng leads (owner: Alejandra).
Design handoff: finalize table UX and approval modal (owner: Ricardo, due 2026-03-12).
Implementation: Backend event model + minimal API endpoints (owner: Marcus, estimate 4 dev days).
Integrate alerting rule into Capacity Dashboard (owner: Priya from Platform).
Run 2-week pilot with Data infra and Console teams starting 2026-03-16; collect adoption metrics.
